title: ODIN Telecom - p95 streaming & fanout discovery
summary: Initial technical discovery for streaming p95 targets, burst fanout behavior, and hosting mode decision (hosted vs dedicated vs private). Customer described real-time call-transcription use case, strict p95 <= 250ms token latency for interactive features, heavy fanout during crisis alerts. Agreed next steps: run a token/sec + streaming benchmark, share security/compliance docs, schedule 2-hour bakeoff with customer data patterns.
topics: p95 latency targets for streaming token generation
concurrency and fanout effects on throughput
hosting mode tradeoffs: Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private (VPC)
benchmark plan: token/sec, streaming p95, multi-region failover
action_items: Maya Chen: send initial pricing sheet + benchmark template by 2026-03-28
Jordan Patel: prepare sample load harness and example k6 script for streaming tests by 2026-03-31
Priya Nair (Odin): share representative prompt sets and traffic distribution CSV by 2026-03-29
next_steps: Redwood to run a 72-hour token/sec streaming probe against a trimmed prompt set (Redwood-hosted test harness)
Customer to review SOC2 report and provide network ACLs for VPC connectivity if private trial is chosen
Schedule 2-hour bakeoff week of 2026-04-06 (deep SE-led benchmarking)
Share model variant + quantization recommendation document
transcript:
[00:00] Maya Chen (AE): hey everyone, thanks for joining. um quick roll call?
[00:06] Lena Strom: lena here. samuel here. priya joining in a sec sorry for the delay.
[00:12] Maya Chen: great, thanks. quick context — we chatted by email, today Jordan from our infra team will dig into latency and streaming specifics. goal: understand your p95 targets, concurrency/fanout, and which hosting mode makes sense.
[00:22] Jordan Patel (SE): hi folks, hi lena, hi samuel. can you walk me through the user journey where low p95 matters? is this conversational, asymmetric bursts, or both?
[00:32] Samuel Rees (CTO): mostly real-time call transcription and live scorecards for call centers. so interactive UI where agents see suggestions live. p95 is the one that kills us — if that spikes past ~250ms per token it starts being noticeable.
[00:44] Priya Nair (SRE): also during incident alerts we fanout summaries to thousands of endpoints, bursty. so sustained steady-state is smaller but fanout is extreme.
[00:55] Maya Chen: ok p95 target ~250ms per token for interactive path and we need to model fanout bursts to ~8k concurrent streams for a short window?
[01:05] Lena Strom: yeah, we estimated about 6–8k simultaneous streaming consumers during an outage. average seq len 120 tokens, but prefix is large — about 200 tokens retained in KV cache.
[01:17] Jordan Patel: that helps. follow-up: where will data live? any residency constraints? PCI/telephony logs?
[01:25] Samuel Rees: EU and NA both, need GDPR controls. not PCI but sensitive PII redaction required. want audit logs, and KMS integration to control keys.
[01:34] Maya Chen: understood. for that we typically recommend Dedicated or Private if you need KMS/HSM + VPC peering. Hosted can work with encrypted-at-rest and customer-managed KMS for some setups but private gives full control.
[01:48] Jordan Patel: architecture question — are you planning to do prefix caching (we call KV/prefix cache) on the platform side or push it into the client? that changes cold start profile.
[01:56] Priya Nair: prefer platform-level caching — we don't want to rehydrate caches on every agent. but we are worried about cost of warm pools and dedicated GPUs.
[02:06] Maya Chen: yep, tradeoff: dedicated warm pools keep p95 down but cost goes up. We have autoscaling with burst capacity and can do canary rollouts for model variants.
[02:16] Jordan Patel: a common pattern for telecom is to use a small dedicated fleet for the interactive lane and fall back to hosted cheaper variants for background jobs. Also multi-region routing — route nearest POP then fallback to central.
[02:27] Samuel Rees: fallback behavior — if dedicated is saturated, we need predictable degradation not timeouts. can Redwood route to a smaller quantized variant with slightly higher latency but lower cost?
[02:36] Jordan Patel: yes, automatic fallback to compatible model variants is supported, and you can define SLO-based policy: e.g., if p95 > 300ms for 30s, route new requests to variant-xq.
[02:47] Lena Strom: curious about streaming p95 measurement — is it per-token or per-chunk? we need to ensure the user sees first token under 300ms and steady streaming doesn't regress.
[02:58] Maya Chen: we measure both. for UI snappiness we look at first-byte latency and per-token p95. we'll include both in the benchmark.
[03:06] Jordan Patel: practical next step — we'd like to run a token/sec streaming probe that simulates your traffic distribution: steady 200 concurrent streams, 8k spike window, seq len distribution you mentioned. can we get your prompts to tune it?
[03:19] Priya Nair: yes we'll share prompt sets — but obv we'll scrub/obfuscate PII. also need to confirm SSO/SAML integration timelines.
[03:28] Samuel Rees: on the security side, SOC2 is a must, and we require per-token audit logs and retention options. is that in Redwood console?
[03:36] Maya Chen: console has token-level traces, per-route dashboards, and audit logs, we can configure retention and export to your SIEM. I'll share SOC2 and sample audit export.
[03:44] Jordan Patel: some lower-level performance Qs — what's your current model and deployment plan? customer-side are you using open models or fine-tuned?
[03:51] Samuel Rees: we plan to use a tuned Llama2 derivative for latency/cost profile. we'll want to try quantization if perf holds up.
[03:58] Jordan Patel: good — runtime selects kernels based on quantization and seq length. quantized models can shave 20–40% token cost but p95 impact depends on CPU/GPU kernel path. we'll validate.
[04:10] Maya Chen: I want to highlight our caching rules — prefix cache reduces repeated token generation and we can pin cache TTL per customer. for call transcription we usually cache shared system prompts and rolling context windows.
[04:22] Priya Nair: what's the cold-start for new sessions if cache miss?
[04:26] Jordan Patel: depends on model and batch sizes. typical cold-start p95 for a 70B model on dedicated warm pool is ~120–180ms per token; hosted shared noisy neighbors can push that to 300–400ms for first tokens.
[04:41] Lena Strom: okay so we probably do dedicated warm pool for interactive, hosted for async. can Redwood support hybrid routing across Hosted/Dedicated?
[04:50] Maya Chen: absolutely — smart routing can send interactive to dedicated, background to hosted; policy is pluggable by route.
[04:57] Samuel Rees: cost question — any ballpark delta between dedicated warm pool vs hosted per 1M tokens?
[05:05] Maya Chen: rough: hosted shared is typically lower per-token (depends on model), dedicated adds fixed infra but yields lower p95 and predictable throughput — we can model economics after we run the benchmark. I'll include a sample TCO sheet.
[05:16] Jordan Patel: another thing — fanout load patterns are network heavy. for Odin's edge POPs, do you need multi-region nodes or can we do central with TCP optimizations?
[05:25] Lena Strom: ideally edge POPs. our architecture already has regional edge proxies. we'd want Redwood nodes in NA/EU to avoid crossing oceans.
[05:32] Maya Chen: we have region routing and can locate tenants on NA/EU-edge clusters. for Private deployments you can bring the inference runtime into your VPC/edge if required.
[05:42] Priya Nair: what about observability — per-route p95 histograms and token counts? we want per-agent telemetry.
[05:48] Jordan Patel: console gives token-level cost + latency breakdown, and we can add tracing hooks. exportable metrics to Prometheus is supported.
[05:55] Samuel Rees: ok, let's talk bench specifics — what's in the benchmark deliverable?
[06:00] Maya Chen: deliverable: p95 per-token time series, first-byte latency, tokens/sec sustained, failure/error rates, CPU/GPU utilization, cold-start/warm-start comparison, fanout spike results and recommended hosting mode.
[06:14] Jordan Patel: timeline: we can stand up the Redwood-hosted probe in 48–72 hours after you give us prompts and traffic CSV. recommended test: 24h steady + injected 10-minute spikes to replicate outage fanout.
[06:26] Lena Strom: that sounds good. what about encryption and KMS — can you use our KMS?
[06:30] Maya Chen: for Dedicated and Private we can integrate with customer-managed KMS/HSM. Hosted can support customer-managed KMS for certain artifacts but Private is the cleanest for full key control.
[06:40] Priya Nair: any red flags on egress or data residency for the test run? we prefer not to send raw audio to external services.
[06:46] Jordan Patel: recommended pattern: customer runs audio pre-processing and turns into text on-prem, then sends textual context for model inference. if you need end-to-end test we can do a private trial in your VPC or redact audio before sending.
[06:58] Samuel Rees: we will prefer text-only for the benchmark; later we can evaluate full audio pass-through on private trial.
[07:04] Maya Chen: noted. quick question for planning — what's your target decision timeline?
[07:09] Lena Strom: internal decision in 6 weeks, pilot running in 8–10 weeks if all goes well.
[07:15] Maya Chen: perfect. we'll prioritize the benchmark and SOC2 docs. Jordan, anything else from infra side?
[07:21] Jordan Patel: two small items — 1) we'll want to measure p95 under multiplexing (multiple sessions per connection) since you do long-lived websockets, 2) we should include KV cache hit/miss ratio in the report.
[07:33] Priya Nair: yes multiplexing is a core optimization for our agents.
[07:36] Jordan Patel: ok will include.
[07:39] Maya Chen: any blockers from your side for the benchmark?
[07:42] Priya Nair: none, we just need your benchmark template and data handling agreement.
[07:47] Maya Chen: will send NDA/TOU - actually we have an engineering data handling note and draft DPA — we'll attach.
[07:54] Samuel Rees: pricing sensitivity — we need a clear delta between keeping dedicated warm pools on 24/7 vs burst-only. can you simulate cost for our expected 2M tokens/day baseline + 10M tokens burst per month?
[08:07] Maya Chen: yep we'll model that in the TCO. I'll add a sensitivity table in the pricing sheet.
[08:14] Lena Strom: one more: audit logs retention — can we set 12 months?
[08:18] Jordan Patel: yes retention is configurable; exporting to your S3 or SIEM is also supported.
[08:23] Maya Chen: great. recap: Redwood runs hosted probe with provided prompts and traffic profile, share SOC2 + DPA, schedule 2hr bakeoff week of 2026-04-06, and Redwood to send pricing + benchmark template.
[08:37] Priya Nair: ok noted. thanks all.
[08:40] Maya Chen: thank you — we'll follow up with calendar invites and the artifacts.
[08:45] Samuel Rees: thanks. bye.
[08:47] Lena Strom: bye.
[08:49] meeting end.
